title: Implement four more-itertools 9.0-era functions at pinned v8.14.0
goal: Clone https://github.com/more-itertools/more-itertools into work/gc-347/repo (relative to the benchmark repo root) and check out pinned commit e2f2d06366a33666c5e97194ad4d5d43e11b8dd9 (release tag v8.14.0); the grader verifies that HEAD equals this exact commit, so keep all repairs as uncommitted working-tree edits to non-test source files. At this commit the package lacks batched, constrained_batches, polynomial_from_roots, and sieve. The sealed tests require all four as public more_itertools exports: fixed-size batching with a short final batch, weight-constrained batching with max_size, max_count, get_len and strict overflow ValueError semantics, expanded polynomial coefficients from roots, and a prime sieve returning primes below n. Each function has independent edge cases, so incremental verification per function is expected. Decompose the work into a written plan, run the grader command first to record the initial RED state and the identities of the failing sealed tests, implement incrementally, and re-run the exact grader command after each increment until all 8 sealed tests pass. Do not edit or shadow anything under assets/gc-347/: the grader re-copies the sealed tests from assets over the workspace and disables pytest plugin autoloading and conftest collection, so test tampering cannot turn the run GREEN.

spec.command: git config --global --add safe.directory '*' && test "$(git -C work/gc-347/repo rev-parse HEAD)" = "e2f2d06366a33666c5e97194ad4d5d43e11b8dd9" && pip -q install pytest==8.2.2 && pip -q install --no-deps ./work/gc-347/repo && rm -rf work/gc-347/sealed_run && mkdir -p work/gc-347/sealed_run && cp assets/gc-347/tests/*.py work/gc-347/sealed_run/ && cd work/gc-347/sealed_run && PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider .

process_expectations: A written repair plan exists at work/gc-347/notes/plan.md before the first source edit, naming the target module(s) and the sealed tests each step is meant to turn green.
The grader command was executed once before any source change and its RED output (failing sealed test identities, not just counts) is preserved verbatim in the run log.
A running log at work/gc-347/notes/attempts.md maps each code iteration to the specific sealed test identities it targeted and what the re-verification run returned.
After any RED re-verification the next diff is traceable to a named failing test, not a blind full rewrite; abandoned approaches are recorded rather than deleted.
An honest cost/time ledger covering all attempts, including failed ones, is kept alongside the notes.
